toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_apps
toolsAdded.description:
List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

- running: is a process for this app live? (pid is 0 when false)
- active: reserved (Linux X11/Wayland focus model differs from frontmost-app); always false.
- kind: `"desktop"` for XDG `.desktop` launcher entries.
- launch_path: the launcher command from `Exec=` (field codes stripped). Pass to `launch_app(launch_path=...)`.

all.description: Also list kernel threads and system daemons (hidden by default).

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_windows

Filter with `app` or `pid`: an unfiltered call lists every window on the host.

pid.description: Only list windows owned by this process ID.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_command
toolsAdded.description: Run a bash command (or a short script) on this computer and get its exit code and output. Use it for terminal, file and document work done in code instead of by clicking: inspect files (ls, cat, head), edit spreadsheets / documents with python3 (openpyxl, odfpy, python-docx, python-pptx when installed), convert with `soffice --headless -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/gui-gate-lo-15520 --convert-to FMT --outdir DIR FILE` (the -env part lets it run while LibreOffice is open). Every command is checked by the gate like a typed terminal command (overwrites, moves, deletes, permission changes and other risky effects need the user's words, the gate's reviewer or a person). If you change a file that is open in an app, reload it there (LibreOffice: File > Reload) or the app's own save will write its old copy over your change. No interactive programs (no editors, pagers or password prompts): stdin is empty. Commands longer than a minute or two: mode=start, then mode=poll.

command.description: bash command line or script (heredocs allowed)

timeout_s.description: seconds before the command is killed (default 30, max 300)

mode.description: run (default): wait for the result. start: launch a long command (installs, downloads, slow scripts) in the background and get a job number at once. poll / stop {job}: its status and output so far / kill it.

job.description: mode=poll / stop: the job number from mode=start

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__check_done
toolsAdded.description: Before you reply DONE, call this once: the gate gathers evidence about the end state (files the task names: exist? changed during this session?; files changed this session; unsaved-document markers; visible Calc cells; terminal tail; open windows; steps the gate refused; your plan's open milestones) and lists possible gaps. It does not judge the task; you decide whether to finish or fix something first.

files.description: extra paths you produced or changed (optional)

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__set_plan
toolsAdded.description: Your own plan and working memory, kept by the gate. Call it once at the start with your feasibility verdict and 2-6 milestones that describe END STATES, not clicks ("report.xlsx is sorted by date and saved", not "click Data > Sort"): feasible:false when the task cannot be done on this computer (the app has no such feature, the thing asked for does not exist, files or hardware are missing, it would need a workaround) - then reply FAIL with the reason. Attach checks the gate can verify without you: checks:[{n:1, check:{file_changed:"~/Desktop/report.xlsx"}}] (file_exists, file_changed, file_contains:[path,text], title_contains, not_title_contains, window_open, app_running, terminal_contains, cell:["B3","value"]). Revise the plan when you learn something (send milestones again; done marks of unchanged milestones are kept). facts:{key: value} stores values you will need later (null deletes). Every action result ends with a one-line progress note; check_done evaluates the checks.

feasible.description: false = this task cannot be done here

facts.description: working memory: {key: value} (value null removes the key)

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_actions
toolsAdded.description:
Batch mode: run several GUI steps in ONE call (single-step tools remain available). Each GUI step is checked by the gate like a single call. Steps, in order:
  {tool, args, expect?}  a GUI action (click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, set_value, ...) or a run_command (its output comes back in the result; a failing command stops the batch). Name things that appear only after an earlier step with args.target = {label, role?}; the gate finds them on screen when the step runs. x/y only in the first GUI step.
  {find: SELECTOR, as: "rows", max?: 20}  read the screen now and keep the matching elements.
  {for_each: "rows", do: [steps]}  repeat steps per element; inside, args.target = "$item" points at it and "$item.label" in any string is its label.
  {if: {exists: SELECTOR} | {not_exists: SELECTOR}, then: [steps], else?: [steps]}
  {read: SELECTOR, as?: "name"}  report the matching elements' labels/values in the result.
SELECTOR = {label} exact, {label_contains}, {label_regex} and/or {role}. The batch stops at the first refused or failed step, when a dialog opens unexpectedly (a popup menu is fine), or when an expect fails ({title_contains} or {new_window: true}). You get what ran plus one fresh read of the window at the end. Max 20 GUI actions. With pick_one:true the steps are alternatives for ONE next action and only the best-rated one runs (use it when you are unsure which way works).

pid.description: Default pid for steps that omit it.

window_id.description: Default window_id for steps that omit it.

steps.description: The program, see the tool description.

pick_one.description: true: the steps are 2-6 ALTERNATIVE candidates for one next action (e.g. a toolbar click, a shortcut, a menu path); the gate runs only the one most likely to work.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__inspect
toolsAdded.description: Read-only look at things other than a window tree (nothing is changed). kind=file {path}: read a file directly - text, PDF, office documents (the saved file's text), images (returned as an image) - instead of writing code to look at it. kind=env {query?}: facts for deciding whether the task is possible here (the paths the task names, installed apps, hardware, python modules). kind=page {query?}: Chrome's open tabs and the current page's text, links and form values (needs Chrome's debugging port). kind=region {pid, window_id, x, y, w, h, scale?}: zoom into part of the window's screenshot. kind=locate {pid, window_id, describe}: find the element matching a description and its element_index/token. kind=howto {query}: how to do something in an app (menu paths, shortcuts, whether the feature exists). kind=memory {query?}: action sequences that worked in earlier runs on similar tasks.

query.description: kind=howto/memory/env/page: what you want to know (page: part of a tab title or URL)

describe.description: kind=locate: the element, e.g. 'the Bold button in the toolbar'
